subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented current-scope limits?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and security, while an open linked PR already carries the implementation path and needs maintainer policy review.

options.title: Review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

options.title: Ship reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress and size guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader native exclude-pattern tracker.

options.title: Defer core expansion
options.body: Document current core backup limits and point optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths only if maintainers explicitly decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The original backup CLI commit lists gumadeiras as co-author/reviewer, which is the strongest history signal for the backup contract decision.
